sourceSpecificRich: Original IM2021 G5 U06:L21 OPTIONAL Weekend Investigation is authentic STUDENT DATA COLLECTION and analysis, not a fixed table of imaginary class observations. Its goal is to define activity categories, express two hours of planned leisure time in FRACTIONS of an hour, and construct teacher-scored line plots from actual participant reports.
Warm-up original Number Talk Fractions of60:1/4×60=15,3/4×60=45,5/4×60=75,9/4×60=135. These represent minutes in fractional hours and prepare children to reason about totals beyond one hour.

Activity1 Data Collection original asks students to IMAGINE two hours of leisure, choose their own activities, write durations in fractional HOURS, and record each duration on appropriate category poster. Source has no prescribed categories, class sizes, individual activity choices or numeric responses. Consent, privacy and classroom practicality assessed by teacher.

Activity2 Data Analysis uses a teacher-assigned poster of REAL student category data; learners construct a line plot and tell a story with at least THREE observations such as total time, min/max range, surprising patterns, number of respondents or fraction below/above one hour. Neither authentic data nor correct storyline can be invented from current teacher HTML.

Previous fictional six-student reading-time demonstration is a labeled Edulytiks extension, never original student data. Exact selected practice tests only the FOUR source number-talk products. Original lesson has no separately printed Cool-down heading; an independently authored exit reflection is OPTIONAL and teacher-scored.
exceptions: Publisher figures/physical learning cards not exact-asset verified; first-party substitutes remain marked
Original gated Cool-down not misrepresented; teacher reviews source mathematical explanations
